In general, the scope of work includes:

• Implementation of all Project Management Plans and Insurances necessary for the works (WH&S, QA, EMP, TMP, Program)

• Provision of appropriate access and environmental controls, including containment measures.

• Removal of degraded concrete by high pressure hydro-demolition.

• Replacement of severely corroded reinforcement bars.

• Reinstatement of concrete.

• Application of silanes to the new concrete surfaces.

• Provision of records and as-constructed information.

publicQuestions.question:
1. There does not seem to have quantities in the BOQ. Drawings have broad quantities (54 piles for instance). Could you please provide all quantities to price accordingly (m2 of repairs per type)

2. The contract mentions liquidated damages in case program is not met. However, it does not seem to have any targeted completion date. Please provide an indication as to when the works are intended to start and intended to be completed.

3. There is a note in the specification making reference to galvashied anodes, however, it is not clear whether or not these are required. Please confirm.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please see below responses to your Request for Information.

1 - A Bill of Quantities has not been published as part of the Tender invitation. Refer to Part C Clause 1.6-1.9. Refer also to Part D, Appendix C, Clause 4.

2 - It is not expected that a timeframe to completion can be accurately determined at the start of the project. Target Completion Date will be determined jointly by the Principal and successful Contractor as the works are underway; as detailed condition survey efforts inform the extent of work to be completed; and as the general rate of progress is established and observed on site by the project team.

3 - Part D, Appendix C, Clause 1.1 makes reference to AS 2239. However, the Specification currently does not require that sacrificial anodes are installed as part of concrete patch repairs. If Tenderers consider this a valuable component of repair methodology, they are invited to provide an optional Rate to Design, Supply and Install anodes (say a Rate per 10 or 20 anodes), for consideration by the Principal. The provision of this optional Rate is not mandatory.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 - Pile Section dimensions, Wharves 5 and 6

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; Appendix E reference drawings 403-003, 403-007, 403-017

The Technical Specification and the Pile Repair Detail at Figure 6 specify a retained core of not less than 250mm x 250mm and reference existing 40mm reinforcing bars, but do not state the overall pile section dimensions.

Of the reference drawings at Appendix E, drawing 303-001 relates to Wharf No. 1 and notes columns of 17" x 19½". Drawing 403-003 is annotated as not proceeded with. Drawing 403-017, which covers the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area, carries the note "WHARF GEOMETRY NOT VERIFIED".

Would the Principal please confirm the pile section dimensions, including corner chamfer, applicable to the piles nominated for repair on Wharves 5 and 6; or confirm that no verified dimensional information is held by the Principal.

Further notes that clause 1.6 states a precise scope of work has not been defined and that the exact extent of repairs will be determined during the Works. Confirmation of the pile section is nonetheless required at tender, as it governs the design and fabrication of reinstatement formwork.

RFI 2 - Release of existing condition survey and investigation reports

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 1.4, 1.5, 7.14; FY26 Works Layout Plan (KBR annotation)

Clause 1.4 of the Scope of Works states that the Priority 1A and 1B defects were identified during a detailed inspection undertaken by KBR in February 2023, that further deterioration has likely occurred since, and that some areas have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey. Clause 7.14 of the Technical Specification quotes concrete cover data attributed to a 1993 report by Beal.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that elements beneath the wharf carry survey markings, and that previously executed repairs are visible, consistent with the 2023 rectification works identified on drawing 300-085.

Would the Principal please make available to all Tenderers the KBR February 2023 detailed inspection report, the 1993 Beal report, and any supporting data relied upon in preparing the FY26 Works Layout Plan, including measured element dimensions, chloride profiles, cover meter surveys, delamination survey results and photographic records.

Would the Principal also please advise which elements have been repaired since the 2023 condition survey, and confirm whether those elements are excluded from the present scope.

RFI 3 - Annexure to the General Conditions of Contract

Reference: Conditions of Contract cl. 18, 20, 26; definitions of LD Cap and Operational Delay Allowance

The General Conditions repeatedly refer to particulars stated in the Annexure, including the Date for Practical Completion, the rate of liquidated damages, the LD Cap, the Operational Delay Allowance, the Defects Liability Period, Security and retention, and required insurance limits.

The Annexure does not appear within Parts A to E of the RFT package. Would the Principal please issue the completed Annexure to all Tenderers.

RFI 4 - Quantities for slab soffit and beam repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(c), cl. 6.1; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Items 3.00 and 4.00

Clause 6.1 states that precise locations and defined areas for slab soffit and beam repairs have not been defined on the drawings. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams by element count.

Part G requires banded rates per square metre, and clause 4.4(c) provides for payment against the final measured area of each individual patch.

Would the Principal please advise the indicative total repair area, in square metres, anticipated for slab soffit repairs and for beam repairs respectively; and the anticipated distribution of individual patch repairs across the area bands set out at clause 4.4(f). If no such estimate is held, would the Principal please confirm this.

RFI 5 - Split of pile repairs between Type A and Type B

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule Item 2.00

Clause 5.5 requires two types of pile repair to be priced. The FY26 Works Layout Plan identifies 54 piles for repair but does not indicate which are anticipated to be Type A and which Type B.

The two repair types differ materially in extent, Type A being one full face over a 2000mm height and Type B extending from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab.

Would the Principal please advise the anticipated number of Type A and Type B pile repairs, or confirm that this allocation is to be determined at the joint inspection under clause 5.2.

RFI 6 - Tenderer access for measurement prior to close of Tender

Reference: Part A — Site Inspection / RFT Briefing; Conditions of Tender cl. 6.2, 6.3

Access at the mandatory Site Inspection on 19 August 2026 was limited to visual observation from the wharf deck. The elements to be repaired are located beneath the wharf deck and were not accessible for inspection or measurement.

Clause 6.2 deems the Tenderer to have inspected the Site and satisfied itself of conditions. In order to discharge that obligation in a meaningful way, would the Principal please confirm in writing whether Tenderers may arrange a further inspection prior to close of Tender with access beneath the wharf deck, including by small vessel, and advise the conditions, notice period, induction and security requirements applicable to such access.

If such access cannot be made available, would the Principal please confirm this in writing.

RFI 7 - Basis of the Principal's estimate of repair extent

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 4.4(d) and Figure 3; cl. 7.9; Conditions of Contract cl. 26

Clause 4.4(d) sets expected repair depths of 150mm for piles, 120mm for slab soffits and 140mm for beams, each with a tolerance of plus or minus 20mm, and provides for rate adjustment where measured depths fall outside that tolerance. Clause 7.9 provides that excessive removal beyond the specified extent is at the Contractor's cost.

Would the Principal please advise the basis on which the expected repair depths at Figure 3 were derived, and confirm whether the Principal anticipates that the actual extent and depth of deterioration may differ materially from those expected values.

Would the Principal further confirm that where measured extents exceed those anticipated to a degree that affects the Contractor's ability to reach Practical Completion by the Date for Practical Completion, the Contractor's entitlement to an extension of time under clause 18 is preserved.

RFI 8 - Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Reference: Part A — RFT Package Details; Technical Specification cl. 4.4

Part A lists Part G Prices and Rates Schedule in Excel format as a returnable document. Would the Principal please confirm that the current issue of Part G, together with Part F Schedules, has been made available to all Tenderers via Vendor Panel, and advise the issue date and revision of each.

RFI 9 - Approved Budget and its relationship to the scope of works

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 1.6, 1.7, 1.8; Conditions of Contract — Date for Practical Completion

Clause 1.7 provides that tendered Fixed Costs and Rates, combined with on-site measurement, will be used to track and forecast project costs up to an approved budget to be advised by the Principal at contract formation. Clause 1.8 provides that the approved budget must not be exceeded by the Contractor unless approved in writing.

The approved budget is therefore not disclosed to Tenderers at the time of pricing, yet governs the volume of work that may be executed under the Contract.

Would the Principal please advise:

(a) the approved budget, or an indicative range, to enable Tenderers to assess the likely volume of work and resource it accordingly;

(b) the mechanism by which the Works will proceed if the approved budget is reached before all nominated elements have been repaired — specifically whether the Contractor is to cease work, whether Practical Completion is achieved at that point, and how Preliminaries are treated for the balance of the Contract period; and

(c) whether the quantities shown on the FY26 Works Layout Plan, being 54 piles, 100 soffit panels, 65 primary beams and 15 secondary beams, are within the approved budget at the Principal's own estimate of rates.

RFI 10 - Pile head haunching and termination of Type B repairs

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 5.5(d); Figure 6 Pile Repair Detail; observed conditions at Site Inspection

Clause 5.5(d) provides that Type B pile repairs shall extend from 1.700m Chart Datum to the underside of the slab. Figure 6 depicts the pile as a prismatic section of constant dimension.

Elouera observed at the Site Inspection that the piles flare into a substantial curved haunch at the pile head, over a significant proportion of the exposed pile height, before meeting the beam soffit. This geometry is not reflected in Figure 6 and appears to vary between piles.

Would the Principal please advise:

(a) whether Type B repairs are required to extend through the haunched pile head to the underside of the slab, or are to terminate below the commencement of the haunch;

(b) if the haunch is included, whether reinstatement of the haunch profile is deemed included in the Type B pile repair rate or is to be measured separately; and

(c) whether any dimensional information for the haunch geometry is held by the Principal.

RFI 11 - Removal of marine growth

Reference: Technical Specification cl. 9.10 Surface Preparation; cl. 14.4 Silane Application; Part G Prices and Rates Schedule

Elouera observed dense marine growth, including oyster and barnacle encrustation, extending a substantial height up the piles from the bed. Removal of this growth is a necessary precursor to hydro-demolition, to reinstatement, and to silane application on any surface within the affected zone.

The Technical Specification addresses surface preparation at clause 9.10 but does not identify removal of marine growth, and no corresponding item is evident in the payment mechanism at clause 4.4.

Would the Principal please confirm whether removal and disposal of marine growth is deemed included within the tendered pile repair rates, or is to be measured and paid separately; and confirm any environmental controls required for its capture and disposal under the Environmental Management Plan.

RFI 12 - Heritage General Exemption Certificate

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 2.1, 2.2

Clause 2.2 provides that work shall not commence until the Principal has confirmed that the General Exemption Certificate — Queensland Heritage Places will apply to this project.

Would the Principal please confirm whether that certificate has been obtained or confirmed as applicable as at the date of tender; and if not, advise the anticipated timing and confirm that any delay to commencement arising from it will be treated as an act or omission of the Principal for the purposes of extension of time under clause 18.

RFI 13 - Hydro-demolition working hours and tidal working windows

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.3(a), 8.3(b); cl. 8.5(b)

Clause 8.3(a) permits working hours between 6.00am and 6.30pm, Monday to Sunday. Clause 8.3(b) provides that there shall be no excessively noisy activities such as hydro-demolition before 8.00am or after 5.00pm, giving an effective nine-hour window for concrete removal.

The elements to be repaired are tidal. Type B pile repairs commence at 1.700m Chart Datum, which the Specification identifies as Mean Sea Level, and are accessible only during low-water windows. Those windows advance by approximately 50 minutes each day and will regularly fall wholly or partly outside the 8.00am to 5.00pm period.

Would the Principal please confirm:

(a) whether the Superintendent will consider approval under clause 8.3(a) for hydro-demolition to be undertaken outside 8.00am to 5.00pm where a low-water working window falls outside those hours, and the basis on which such approval would be assessed; and

(b) whether any noise limits, monitoring requirements or conditions apply, having regard to nearby residential receivers.

RFI 14 - Maritime Security Identification Cards

Reference: Scope of Works cl. 8.2(g); General Conditions of Contract cl. 7.3

Clause 8.2(g) of the Scope of Works states that it is expected Maritime Security Identification Cards will not be required, as the works are being undertaken around vessel operations.

Clause 7.3(a) of the General Conditions provides that if the work is required to be performed in maritime security zones, at least two employees of the Contractor must hold an MSIC, with all associated costs borne by the Contractor.

Would the Principal please confirm which position applies to these works, and whether any part of the Wharf 5 and Wharf 6 works area is designated a maritime security zone.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Queensland Mental Health Commission (the Commission) is a statutory body established under the Queensland Mental Health Commission Act 2013 to drive systemic reform across Queensland’s mental health, alcohol and other drugs, and suicide prevention systems. A core function of the Commission is to develop and facilitate implementation of a whole-of-government strategic plan to improve mental health and wellbeing outcomes for Queenslanders. The current plans, Shifting minds: The Queensland Mental Health, Alcohol and Other Drugs, and Suicide Prevention Strategic Plan 2023-2028 (Shifting minds) and its associated sub-plans; The Queensland Trauma Strategy 2024-2029, Achieving balance: The Queensland Alcohol and Other Drugs Plan 2022-2027 and Every life: The Queensland Suicide Prevention Plan 2019-2029 Phase Two, provides the overarching framework for this work.

In addition, in response to Recommendation 19 of the 2022 Queensland Parliament Mental Health Select Committee Inquiry into opportunities to improve mental health outcomes for Queenslanders, Thriving Lives, Connected Communities – Queensland’s Commitment to Mental Health and Wellbeing (Thriving Lives, Connected Communities) was developed to provide a focused direction for improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Recommendation 19 – Develop Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy

The committee recommends the Queensland Government considers the development of a population based Mental Health and Wellbeing Strategy that works across human services portfolios and is aimed at improving community mental health and wellbeing.

Time-limited, non-recurrent funding has been provided to the Commission to progress priorities identified in Thriving Lives, Connected Communities.

In 2025, the Commission delivered the Mental Health and Wellbeing Grants program, (the Grants) distributing $2.8 million across 22 projects to strengthen community mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion, prevention and early intervention initiatives.

Building on the Grants, the Commission established the Mental Health and Wellbeing Investment Package (the Package), a targeted, time-limited investment of $9 million that adopts a strategic and coordinated approach. The Package supports initiatives that strengthen population-based mental health and wellbeing through mental health promotion and prevention, while leveraging existing systems, infrastructure and partnerships to maximise impact, reduce duplication and support sustainability beyond the funding period.

publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Sophie,

The Commission may have existing networks and engagement mechanisms that could be drawn upon to support Lived-Living Expertise involvement. However, suppliers should propose an approach to engaging people with Lived-Living Expertise, in line with the ITO requirements, that aligns with their proposed methodology and approach to the evaluation.

Queensland Mental Health Commission

publicQuestions.question: The Commission requires remuneration of engaged LLE participants. Should these costs be included within the supplier's proposed budget, or will the Commission manage these costs separately? If suppliers are expected to budget for participation, can the Commission provide guidance regarding the anticipated number and frequency of LLE engagement activities over the course of the evaluation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Sophie,

As outlined in Part A (Section 1.2) of the ITO, the Supplier is required to provide remuneration to people with Lived-Living Expertise engaged in consultation, collaboration or co-design, at a minimum, in line with the Commission’s paid participation rates.

In addition, the Selection Criteria (refer to Parts A and C of the ITO) specify that “the Supplier’s budget must reflect appropriate allocation to personnel, engagement (including paid participation for people with Lived-Living Expertise) and reporting.” Suppliers should therefore include costs associated with paid participation within their proposed budget.

The Selection Criteria also require suppliers to demonstrate “how people with Lived-Living Expertise will be involved throughout all stages of the evaluation, including its design, delivery, interpretation of findings and knowledge translation.”

The ITO has not prescribed a specific number or frequency of engagement activities. Suppliers should propose an approach to Lived-Living Expertise involvement in line with the ITO requirements, that is appropriate to their proposed project and evaluation methodology.

Kind regards,

Jasmine Repia

Queensland Mental Health Commissions

title: RFT260086 - Long-Term Residual Waste Solution — Standardised Site Assessment
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) invites suitably qualified consultants to submit tenders for RFT260086 – Long-Term Residual Waste Solution – Standardised Site Assessment.

The engagement is for a strategic waste planning consultancy to undertake a comprehensive, evidence-based assessment of Council's long-term (30–50 year) residual waste disposal solution. The successful consultant will reconcile the remaining life of the existing Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility, model long-term residual waste demand, develop a standardised assessment methodology, evaluate potential long-term disposal options against the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), and prepare a defensible options report to inform future Council decision-making.

This is a desktop strategic planning and technical assessment. It does not include detailed engineering design, statutory approvals, land acquisition, or intrusive field investigations, whic...

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Thursday 10 September 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) operates the Lochlees Resource Recovery and Landfill Facility at Emerald as its principal regional residual waste disposal facility. With the remaining capacity of the existing landfill being finite, Council is undertaking strategic planning to identify the most appropriate long-term (30–50 year) residual waste solution for the region. This procurement forms part of that strategic planning process and does not represent a decision to develop or acquire any particular site.

Tenderers should demonstrate experience in strategic landfill planning, waste infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and multi-criteria options analysis within the Queensland regulatory environment. Experience applying the Queensland Landfill Siting, Design, Operation and Rehabilitation Guideline (ESR/2015/1627), landfill capacity modelling, life-cycle costing, GIS-based spatial assessment, and facilitation of strategic decision-making for local government or similar organisations will be highly regarded.

Council will provide relevant background information, including previous investigations, landfill survey information, airspace and stockpile data, waste generation information, existing planning studies and other reference material identified within the tender documentation. Tenderers are expected to validate and appropriately use this information while exercising independent professional judgement.

The successful consultant will be required to:

- Work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Attend key project meetings and undertake site inspections at Emerald where required.

- Provide all reports, models and supporting documentation in fully editable electronic formats.

- Develop a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment methodology.

- Cooperate with an independently appointed peer reviewer engaged separately by Council for review of the assessment methodology.

The engagement is a professional services consultancy only. Intrusive field investigations, statutory approvals, detailed engineering design, land acquisition activities and other downstream implementation works are expressly excluded from this procurement and, if required, will be commissioned under separate engagements.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a consultant that can deliver a transparent, evidence-based and independently defensible assessment of long-term residual waste disposal options that will support future strategic decision-making.

The successful consultant should:

- Deliver a robust, standardised assessment methodology capable of objectively comparing all reasonable long-term residual waste options on a consistent basis.

- Produce clear, high-quality technical reports and supporting models that are fully editable and suitable for future refinement and downstream planning.

- Demonstrate a sound understanding of Queensland landfill planning, environmental constraints, waste infrastructure planning and strategic options assessment.

- Apply recognised industry best practice and relevant Queensland regulatory guidance throughout the engagement.

- Provide practical, well-reasoned recommendations supported by documented assumptions, analysis and evidence.

- Maintain proactive communication, meet agreed project milestones, and work collaboratively with Council's project team throughout the engagement.

- Respond constructively to Council feedback and the independently commissioned methodology peer review within the agreed programme.

- Deliver all services within the agreed fixed lump-sum fee and project timeframe.

Council is seeking a consultant capable of becoming a trusted strategic advisor for this engagement by combining strong technical capability with practical understanding of local government decision-making, risk management and long-term infrastructure planning. The successful outcome will provide Council with a defensible evidence base to support future decisions regarding its long-term residual waste disposal strategy, while recognising that this engagement does not commit Council to any particular site, development or capital project.

title: Pick of the Crop 2027-28 expansion to Far North Queensland
description:
HWQld is Queensland’s dedicated prevention agency established to prevent chronic disease and improve health equity, with a focus on healthy eating, physical activity and obesity.

HWQld has committed to implementing a whole-school healthy eating program in all state primary schools across Queensland to increase children’s vegetable and fruit consumption. Pick of the Crop (POTC) is a whole school, multi-strategic, evidence-based healthy eating initiative developed by HWQld; it is flexible and designed by schools to focus on their unique community needs and school environment. 

HWQld seeks to engage one or more Implementation partner/s in a two-year agreement to support delivery of POTC across Far North Queensland's Department of Education (DoE) regions.

Implementation Partner/s will be responsible for recruiting and managing a regional coordinator and supporting school engagement, implementation and stakeholder collaboration.

Key activities are expected to include:<br...

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Friday 18 September 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
POTC is a tried and test model, demonstrated to be feasible for schools and teachers to implement and resulting in changes to students’ attitudes and beliefs towards vegetables and fruit consistent with project objectives.

Program need

Most Queensland (Qld) children do not meet the Australian Dietary Guideline recommendations:

 •	Only 3.2% of Queensland children aged 5 to 11 years are eating the recommended amount of 5 vegetables every day.

 •	80.7% of children eat the recommended 2 serves of fruit every day.

 •	39% of total energy intake of 4 to 8-year old males and 36% of females comes from unhealthy food and drinks.

 •	In 2022, research commissioned by HWQld found that children born in Queensland in 2023 could lose up to 4 years of life expectancy if obesity rates are not reversed, increasing up to 5 years for First Nations children.

Schools are ideal settings to reach large numbers of children, their families and communities and can shape their values and foster lifelong habits.

The overall goal of POTC is to achieve a sustained increase in vegetable and fruit consumption among primary school aged children in Queensland.

HWQld Strategic Alignment

POTC started with 35 state (primary) schools in three regional areas (Bowen, Bundaberg and Logan) as a pilot in 2021 to support HWQld’s commitment to increasing vegetable and fruit consumption for Queensland’s children, and since then has grown to reach 300 state schools with more than 70,000 student enrolments across Queensland. The vision for POTC is for all Queensland primary schools to have an opportunity to implement POTC by 2032.

title: Palm Island Waste Transfer Facility – Design & Construction
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking suitably qualified and experienced Tenderers to undertake the design and construction of the Palm Island Waste Transfer Facility (WTF).

The Works include completion of detailed design and all investigations, approvals, certifications, procurement, supply, construction, services and utility connections, testing, commissioning, handover and close-out necessary to deliver a complete and operational Waste Transfer Facility in accordance with Part B – Specification.

The Invitation to Tender also includes the Men's Shed as separately priced Optional Works. Council may, at its sole discretion and subject to funding availability, elect to include all or part of the Optional Works in the Contract. The pricing or availability of the Optional Works does not alter the Tenderer's obligation to submit a complete and conforming Tender for the mandatory Waste Transfer Facility Works.

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Wednesday 23 September 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Council is progressing the development of a new Waste Transfer Facility within the existing waste-management area on Palm Island.

Council has commissioned a concept design for the facility. The concept design is provided as reference information and establishes Council's intended functional arrangement and project outcomes. The Contractor remains responsible for verifying the concept, undertaking all investigations required for its design and developing a complete detailed design satisfying the Contract.

The concept design includes demolition/site clearance, roads and hardstand areas, the main waste roof structure and concrete floor, push/barrier walls, relocation/reconstruction of existing Containers for Change infrastructure, perimeter fencing, leachate infrastructure and a demountable office facility.

Council's Planning Scheme identifies the Waste Transfer Facility as a Utility Installation and Council has received advice that the proposed use is Accepted Development where the applicable Planning Scheme requirements are satisfied. The Contractor remains responsible for reviewing the Planning Scheme and ensuring that its design and construction comply with all applicable requirements.

The proposed works are to remain within the existing disturbed operational area and avoid disturbance to mapped regulated vegetation. The Contractor must verify and appropriately manage all environmental constraints applicable to its design and construction.

Council is separately procuring operational waste-management equipment. The procurement and supply of that equipment are excluded from the mandatory D&C scope; however, all permanent infrastructure, utility services and interfaces required for the operation of the facility and the relevant equipment categories are included.

Council is also progressing the Development Application for the Men's Shed Optional Works. Council remains responsible for that DA process. If the Optional Works are accepted, the Contractor must comply with the resulting approval and conditions and obtain all remaining approvals and certifications required for its design and construction.

The selection of a Tenderer as a pre-qualified supplier entitles the Principal to engage the Tenderer during the Term without first seeking quotes or tenders but does not give rise to any obligation on the Principal to do so. Selection as a pre-qualified supplier does not guarantee that the Tenderer will be engaged to provide any, or any minimum quantity or value of, services. The engagement of a successful Tenderer will be at the Principal’s sole discretion based on operational requirements.

Suppliers who were successfully appointed to the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Trade and Professional Services in 2024 and 2025 are not required to submit a Tender again this year, as this is the same register. This process provides an opportunity for those not currently on the register, to submit a Tender for inclusion.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

I am reaching out regarding the Pest Control Tender for Cassowary Coast Council. To prepare an accurate and competitive quote, I kindly request the site maps and measurements for all relevant structures and buildings included in this tender.

Having access to the layout and dimensions will allow me to correctly scope the work and ensure all areas are appropriately covered in the submission.

Please advise if any additional documentation is available, such buildings lists, access notes, or previous services schedules.

Thank you, and I look forward to your response.

Kind regards,

Jason Stack

Pest Pro Exterminators
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

Thank you for your enquiry.

This tender for the Register of Prequalified Suppliers (COW000099) will assess capable suppliers to provide the services listed in Part 2 - Scope across the Cassowary Coast Region. The pricing schedule for this register does not require site-specific pricing. Instead, respondents are asked to provide general rates, such as hourly labour rates and any applicable travel or call-out charges, to support Council’s assessment of suppliers for general works as required.

The category for pest control works includes internal and external pest treatments, vermin and reptile removal. Submissions should consider the information provided in Part 2 - Scope and pricing schedule must be provided in the excel format requested by the Principal.

Kind Regards,

The Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
Please provide a detailed description of the “Electrical Services & Project Management” category as stated in the scope document.

Additionally, please provide a complete list of the equipment required for testing and calibration, including the relevant specifications where applicable.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

Thank you for your enquiry.

As defined in Part 2 - Scope, the categories include the below services:

- Electrical Services: General electrical works (including testing and calibration) and industrial electrical works – e.g. switchboard manufacturing, PLC Installation / programming, SCADA, industrial wiring and controls; and

- Project Management: Provision of project management services.

Council is unable to advise on the specific equipment, materials or methodology that individual respondents may choose to use. Respondents are encouraged to consider Part 2 - Scope and determine the resources and approach they consider appropriate for delivery of the services. The supplier may choose to select the categories which are most relevant to the services the business provides.

Submissions should consider the information provided in Part 2 - Scope and pricing schedule must be provided in the excel format requested by the Principal. For your business to submit your schedule of rates in a more suitable manner, you may enter additional information within each cell, including pricing as relevant.

Kind Regards,

The Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement team,

To assist respondents in preparing accurate and value-for-money rates under the Schedule of Rates, could Council please clarify how it expects work to be issued under this Register?

We understand the Register does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of work, and that suppliers may be engaged on a case-by-case basis according to Council’s operational requirements.

For trade categories such as electrical services, testing/calibration, solar and energy services, maintenance and related repair works, can Council confirm whether engagement is expected to be primarily through individual call-outs / work orders using the submitted hourly rates, or whether Council may also issue defined packages of work where quantities, asset counts, locations or service frequencies are known?

Where Council has recurring or planned maintenance requirements, is it anticipated that suppliers may be invited to provide a separate lump sum, fixed price or package rate for that defined scope, rather than relying only on the standard hourly Schedule of Rates?

If available, could Council also provide any indicative historical work order volumes, typical service types, or broad category/zone-based demand for electrical, maintenance and solar/energy services? This would help respondents price more accurately, account for zone coverage and availability, and avoid building unnecessary contingency into hourly rates.

Thanks.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council operates a decentralised procurement model, with individual departments and officers responsible for procuring goods and services based on their operational requirements.

At this stage, Council is unable to confirm the specific nature, quantity, frequency or method of procurement for future requirements under the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Trade and Professional Services, as the Register does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of work.

Future individual requirements will be procured in accordance with Council’s applicable procurement processes, having regard to the nature and value of the requirement. This may include engagement through the Register or through another appropriate procurement process.

Council is unable to provide historical work volumes or indicative future demand for these services.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We are considering applying for inclusion on this Register, however the listed insurance requirements are vastly in excess of the norm for our profession and the scope of work that we undertake.

We are a drafting consultancy and our only deliverables are drawings for steel fabrication, provided on paper or electronically. Consequently our Public Liability risk amounts to little more than an occasional paper cut. Therefore the $20m PL requirement is vastly in excess of the norm for our profession and the cost of increasing ours to that amount would be too onerous to entertain given that there is no assurance of any particular volume of work.

Similarly, although our successfully completed projects have included several major and renowned high-rise buildings, an offshore naval facility, ferry terminals, port and harbour restructuring, shopping centres and similar, our worst-case Professional Indemnity liability is unlikely to ever rise above perhaps $100k, due to the nature of independent checks during the process. All of our output is Checked and Reviewed prior to the fabrication of the steel, by the Architect and Engineer responsible for the project, so any major discrepancies would be corrected at that stage.

A drafting consultancy that engages in projects of the size and scope that we do, would not normally carry PL insurance of more than $5m and PI insurance of $1m, if at all. More than that is excessive for the extent of risk that might ever be encountered, and is also too costly to be viable.

Therefore the question is - can Council vary the insurance requirement on a case-by-case basis, or should we not unnecessary spend our, and Council's, time making and processing this Application?

If the insurance is not variable it would be very unfortunate because over the last 25 years we have built a reputation for providing meticulous product at a price that is more than competitive in our industry

Thank you and kind regards.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

Thank you for your enquiry and for providing further information regarding your business.

Council advises that the requirement for Public Liability and Professional Indemnity Insurance is not able to be varied on a case-by-case basis and is outlined at sections 2.3 and 6.3 of Part 2. Scope.

Section 6.3 states:

“The supplier must effect and maintain the following insurances in accordance with the requirements listed for each category at section 2.3:

1.	Public liability insurance in the amount of at least $20,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;

2.	Professional indemnity insurance in the amount of at least $5,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;”

Please refer to section 2.3 to confirm the minimum requirement for insurances at each category.

We appreciate your comments and interest in our procurement and look forward to reviewing your submission should you choose to submit.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

Clause 22.1(a) of the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services limits the aggregate liability of each party to that party's Liability Limit, and clause 1.1(ee)(ii) defines the Supplier's Liability Limit as the amount stated in the SEO. Could Council please confirm what amount, if any, it intends to state as the Liability Limit in Supplier Engagement Orders issued under this register, and whether a standard figure will apply across the register or whether it will be set for each engagement?

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

Part 3, Schedule F1 asks respondents to provide details of any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures "to the Contract contained in Part 4 - Contract or the scope contained in Part 5 - Scope of the Request for Tender". In this Request for Tender, Part 2 is the Scope and Part 4 is the Schedule of Rates. Could Council please confirm that departures should be recorded against the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services (Issue LGT2.4, October 2025) and Part 2. Scope?

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Section 5.3 of Part 2 - Scope requires hourly rates to be charged inclusive of GST, and the Part 4 column headings read "GST Inc". Clause 5.3 of the Procurement Process Conditions requires the Price to be submitted exclusive of GST, and clause 16.10 of the Standard Terms and Conditions provides that the amount payable for a supply is to be increased by the amount of any GST imposed. Council has previously confirmed that rates are to be submitted GST inclusive. Could Council please also confirm that no further GST will be added to those rates on invoice under clause 16.10?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

This Arrangement does not, in itself, constitute a contract for the provision of Goods and/or Services, and therefore a liability limit is not predetermined for future procurements.

Clause 1.1(ee) Liability Limit and Clause 1.1(xx) SEO (from ‘Supplier Engagement Order’) provide the mechanism for the applicable liability limit to be established for each future procurement, with the Supplier’s liability determined in accordance with Clause 1.1(ee) and the relevant SEO.

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

The references to Part 4 – Contract and Part 5 – Scope are to the respective Parts identified in the Request for Tender documentation. Respondents are to record any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures against the relevant Contract and Scope documents identified in the Request for Tender.

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Council advises that, for the purposes of completing the Schedule of Rates, all rates are to be submitted inclusive of GST, as indicated in Part 4 – Schedule of Rates, where the relevant rate columns are identified as “Rate (Inc GST)”.

Accordingly, Respondents should ensure that their tendered rates are inclusive of GST. For clarity, the Schedule of Rates is to be relied upon in determining the required GST treatment of the tendered rates, and the rates submitted are not to have GST added again on invoicing.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
We are preparing a proposal in response to City of Boroondara, Invitation to Supply -Service Review Framework, Contract No. 2026/164, issued 1 September 2026 (Parts A, B, C and D) and welcome the opportunity to do so. In accordance with clause 2.2 of Part B.2 -Council Requirements, we submit the following requests for clarification and further information through VendorPanel for the attention of the Project Manager.

Several of the matters below concern apparent discrepancies or omissions within the Invitation documents. We raise them in accordance with our obligation under clause 1.2(b) of Part B.2 to notify Council in writing of any discrepancy, ambiguity, error or inconsistency, so that Council has a fair opportunity to consider what corrective action, if any, is necessary. We understand that Council is under no obligation to respond, and that responses of general application may be issued to all suppliers as part of the Invitation.

Timetable and process

1.	Which cut-off date applies to requests for clarification? The VendorPanel Request Summary (Reference D) states 5:00pm, Tuesday 8 September 2026, while Item 8 of Part A.1 states 14 September 2026 as the end of the period for questions or requests for information.

2.	Please confirm the intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier. Item 8 of Part A.1 states 2 October 2026, while VendorPanel records a decision date of 29 September 2026.

3.	Does Council intend to hold a briefing session under clause 2.3 of Part B.2? Item 7 of Part A.1 has not been populated and no briefing has been advertised on VendorPanel. If a session is to be held, please advise the date, time and format.

Evaluation, response format and lodgement

4.	What weighting is applied to each of the evaluation criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1, and how is the demonstration of sustainable and social procurement impact weighted relative to price and to professional competence, capacity and experience?

5.	Is a page limit or word limit to be applied to the proposal? Clause 3.4(c) of Part B.2 refers to limits "where specified", but no limit is specified in the Invitation or in Part D. If a limit applies, please confirm whether it extends to supplementary material and curricula vitae.

6.	Should the seven questions posed by Council within VendorPanel be answered in VendorPanel, within Part D - The Proposal, or in both? We also seek Council's guidance on where the reverse brief required by Part A.2 should be presented, as Part D contains no corresponding field.

7.	Part D refers to the completion and return of the COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form. That form was not included in the documents issued with the Invitation. Please provide the form, or confirm whether it is required for an engagement of this nature.

Mandatory requirements

8.	Is RapidGlobal registration applicable to this engagement? If so, please confirm at what stage of the process registration and accreditation are required.

9.	Please confirm the insurance limits required for this engagement. Clause 6.3 of Part C requires public liability cover of not less than $10,000,000 and professional indemnity cover of not less than $5,000,000, each with a principal's indemnity extension, while the insurance schedule in Part D retains placeholder values ("$XXML") and includes product liability and WorkCover fields that may not be applicable to a consultancy engagement.

Scope, pilot and Part 2

10.	Has Council established a budget envelope or Maximum Spend Amount for Part 1, and separately for the optional Part 2?

11.	Item 8 of Part A.1 records the indicative timeframe for Part 2 as "6-8". Please confirm whether this is expressed in weeks or in months.

12.	How and when will the small Council service for the Part 1.B pilot be nominated, and what indicative information can Council provide regarding its scale, budget, staffing and the maturity of its performance and financial data?

13.	What Council resourcing will be made available to the provider during the engagement, including a project sponsor, a working group or steering forum, service owner and staff availability, and access to service performance, financial, workforce and customer data, particularly during the six-week pilot?

14.	What is the current status and expected completion date of Council's Service Catalogue, and how firm is Council's present intention to proceed with Part 2?

15.	Are the nine draft Service Review Guardrails at Reference B settled, or does Council expect the successful provider to test and refine them as part of Part 1.A?

16.	Does Council have an existing service review methodology, template or completed review that the Framework must align with, build upon or replace? If the structure of the developing Service Catalogue is available, would Council make it available to inform the design of the Framework?

17.	Beyond the July 2026 Overview at Reference C, is the full Benefits Management Framework available to respondents, including benefit domains, headline benefits, the KPI and measure library, and any benefit register or reporting templates? Alignment with the Benefits Framework is an express requirement of Part A.2.

Proposed Contract (Part C)

18.	Clause 6.2 of Part B.2 provides that the successful supplier must enter into a contract on the basis of its proposal without negotiation, while Part D invites suppliers to state departures from Part C, which Council will risk assess and which "will be subject to negotiations". Please confirm how departures stated in the Part D compliance table will be treated during evaluation, and whether the statement of a departure affects a proposal's conformity.

Would Council consider granting the successful provider a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the general methodology and generic templates for commercial purposes, excluding all Council-specific, confidential and identifying content?

20.	The Framework is intended to provide the basis for establishing a panel of suitably qualified providers to undertake future service reviews. Please confirm whether the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework will be eligible to respond to that subsequent panel approach to market, or whether Council would regard that as a conflict of interest precluding participation.

21.	Clause 3.3 of Part C contemplates that "Contract retentions shall be made where applicable". Please confirm whether Council intends to apply any retention to payments under this contract and, if so, on what basis.

publicQuestions.answer:
Council thanks the supplier for its clarification questions in relation to City of Boroondara Invitation to Supply – Service Review Framework, Contract No. 2026/164. Council provides the following responses for the assistance of suppliers in preparing proposals. These responses should be read together with the Invitation documents and any addenda or clarifications issued through VendorPanel.

Timetable and process

1. Which cut-off date applies to requests for clarification?

Council confirms that the applicable cut-off date for requests for clarification is 14 September 2026, as stated in Item 8 of Part A.1 of the Invitation. Council will update or clarify VendorPanel records if required.

2. Please confirm the intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier.

The intended date for formal notification of the successful supplier is 2 October 2026, as stated in Item 8 of Part A.1. This date is indicative and may be varied by Council in accordance with the Invitation conditions.

3. Does Council intend to hold a briefing session under clause 2.3 of Part B.2?

Council does not currently intend to hold a briefing session. Suppliers should submit any clarification questions through VendorPanel by the applicable cut-off date.

Evaluation, response format and lodgement

4. What weighting is applied to each of the evaluation criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1?

Council has not published individual weightings for the evaluation criteria. Proposals will be assessed having regard to the criteria listed in Item 10 of Part A.1, including professional competence, capacity and experience, price, risk, mandatory requirements, sustainable and social procurement impact, and the overall value for money proposition.

5. Is a page limit or word limit to be applied to the proposal?

No specific page or word limit has been specified in the Invitation documents. Suppliers should ensure their proposal is complete, concise and directly responsive to the requirements. Supplementary material and curricula vitae may be included where relevant.

6. Should the seven questions posed by Council within VendorPanel be answered in VendorPanel, within Part D – The Proposal, or in both?

Suppliers should answer the VendorPanel questions in VendorPanel as required. The reverse brief required by Part A.2 should also be included in the supplier’s proposal submission as a clearly labelled section, either within Part D where most appropriate or as an attachment to the proposal.

7. Part D refers to the COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form, which was not included.

The COMP 002 notification of risks and hazards form is not required for this engagement because RapidGlobal registration is not required.

Mandatory requirements

8. Is RapidGlobal registration applicable to this engagement?

No. Council confirms, following advice from Council’s OHS representative, that RapidGlobal registration is not required for this engagement.

9. Please confirm the insurance limits required for this engagement.

The required insurance limits are those stated in clause 6.3 of Part C: public liability insurance of not less than $10,000,000 for any single occurrence and professional indemnity insurance of not less than $5,000,000 for any single occurrence. Product liability and WorkCover requirements apply only where relevant to the supplier’s circumstances and the nature of the services.

Scope, pilot and Part 2

10. Has Council established a budget envelope or Maximum Spend Amount for Part 1, and separately for the optional Part 2?

Council has not disclosed a budget envelope for Part 1 or the optional Part 2. Suppliers should provide a value-for-money proposal with clear pricing for Part 1 and separate pricing for the optional Part 2.

11. Item 8 of Part A.1 records the indicative timeframe for Part 2 as “6–8”. Please confirm whether this is expressed in weeks or months.

The intended timeframe for Part 2 is 6–8 weeks, subject to the supplier’s proposed approach and Council’s decision whether to proceed.

12. How and when will the small Council service for the Part 1.B pilot be nominated?

The small Council service for the pilot will be nominated by Council in consultation with the successful supplier during project initiation. Council will provide relevant information about the nominated service at that time, including available performance, financial, workforce and customer data where relevant and available.

13. What Council resourcing will be made available to the provider during the engagement?

Council will make appropriate project governance and subject matter input available, including access to relevant Council stakeholders and data where available. The detailed governance structure, including sponsor, working group or steering arrangements, will be confirmed with the successful supplier during project initiation.

14. What is the current status and expected completion date of Council’s Service Catalogue, and how firm is Council’s present intention to proceed with Part 2?

Council’s Service Catalogue is currently under development and expected to be completed by December 2026. Part 2 is optional, not guaranteed, and will proceed only at Council’s discretion following completion of Part 1 and when the Service Catalogue is sufficiently developed to support the work.

15. Are the nine draft Service Review Guardrails settled?

The nine Service Review Guardrails are draft and should be treated as guiding principles. Council expects the successful provider to have regard to them and may test and refine their practical application through Part 1.A and the pilot.

16. Does Council have an existing service review methodology, template or completed review that the Framework must align with, build upon or replace?

Council is seeking the development of a practical, fit-for-purpose Service Review Framework and associated tools. Any existing relevant materials or examples will be made available to the successful supplier where appropriate. If available and suitable, the developing Service Catalogue structure may also be shared to inform the Framework design.

17. Beyond the July 2026 Overview at Reference C, is the full Benefits Management Framework available to respondents?

Attachment 2 provides Council’s Benefits Framework for the purposes of this Invitation. Further Benefits Framework materials, including benefit domains, measures, registers or reporting templates, may be provided to the successful supplier where available and relevant to the engagement.

Proposed Contract (Part C)

18. Please confirm how departures stated in the Part D compliance table will be treated during evaluation.

Suppliers must clearly state any departures from Part C in the relevant compliance table. Departures will be considered as part of Council’s evaluation and risk assessment. The inclusion of a departure does not automatically make a proposal non-conforming, but Council may take the nature and extent of any departure into account when assessing risk and value for money.

19. Would Council consider granting the successful provider a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the general methodology and generic templates for commercial purposes?

Council’s position is as set out in Part C of the Proposed Contract. Suppliers may identify any proposed departure or alternative wording in their compliance response. Council will consider any proposed departure as part of its evaluation and risk assessment.

20. Please confirm whether the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework will be eligible to respond to a subsequent panel approach to market.

Council does not intend to automatically preclude the provider engaged to develop and pilot the Framework from participating in any future panel procurement. Any participation would be subject to the requirements of the future procurement process and appropriate management of any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest.

21. Please confirm whether Council intends to apply any retention to payments under this contract.

Council does not currently intend to apply a payment retention under this contract unless otherwise specified in the final contract or required in the circumstances.

Council trusts these responses assist suppliers in preparing proposals ahead of the closing time of 5:00pm on 22 September 2026.

Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access.

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so?

publicQuestions.answer:

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it? This system is fitted and operation on all existing units

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access. Our existing cards are HID Prox. Our existing Mix Telematics system and all other systems that utilise our employee RFID cards can use all 3 of these credential types

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so? publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon

Item 1, Control and SCADA Scope

Reference: Technical Specification (Part 2, Appendix A) Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "SCADA and PLC".

The tender documents appear to conflict on responsibility for the control and SCADA scope:

•	The Technical Specification (Sections 15.1.1 and 15.1.2) requires the Contractor to perform all SCADA configuration, RTU and control programming, program the PLC and RTU, integrate the station into Council's SCADA system, produce a Functional Specification, and fully commission the telemetry system.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state the Contractor supplies the unprogrammed MIRI and PLC, Council returns them programmed, and the Contractor will not program or integrate the switchboard.

Please confirm who is responsible for the control and SCADA scope, specifically the PLC and MIRI programming, SCADA integration, and the Functional Specification deliverable (Section 15.1.2).

If any of these remain the Contractor's responsibility, please advise Council's preferred SCADA integrator.

Item 2, Groundwater Level for Dewatering

Reference: Geotechnical Report (Part 2, Appendix E, GE_2510.1180) Sections 5 and 6.2.3; PPR Section 2.6; Site Meeting Minutes dated 20/08/2026, "Geotechnical Conditions and Dewatering".

The tender documents give conflicting groundwater levels:

•	The Geotechnical Report states groundwater was encountered at 8.0m in BH1, records this as the groundwater table in Table 5.1, and adopts 8.0m as the basis for its trench stability assessment in Section 6.2.3.

•	The Site Meeting Minutes (20/08/2026) state groundwater may be encountered approximately 1 to 2 metres below ground level.

The 1 to 2 metre figure does not appear in the Geotechnical Report or elsewhere in the tender documents. Given the deep excavations in the scope, this difference has a significant impact on dewatering design, methodology and price.

Please confirm the groundwater level tenderers are to adopt as the basis for pricing dewatering and excavation.

If the 1 to 2 metre level is to be adopted, please provide the supporting investigation data, confirm whether the Geotechnical Report's trench stability and excavation recommendations remain valid, and advise how dewatering is to be allowed for this condition.

Regards
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI Response – Control and SCADA Scope

The Contractor shall:

* Supply the unprogrammed MIRI and HMI to Council.

Council shall:

* Provide a programmed MIRI and HMI to the Contractor.

The Contractor shall:

* Install the programmed MIRI and HMI into the switchboard.

* Test and install the switchboard into position on site and connect all site equipment as per the design.

* Not be required to produce a Functional Specification

This above scope will alleviate the contractor from having to perform SCADA integration because the equipment will come pre-programmed.

RFI Response – Groundwater Level for Dewatering

The geotechnical investigation recorded free groundwater in BH1 at approximately 8.0 m below ground level at the time of investigation.

The reference in the Site Meeting Minutes to groundwater potentially being encountered at approximately 1-2 m below ground level, as the Liquid Limit of soil is around 44%-50%, indicates the moist soil may encounter water at shallow depth. The groundwater conditions may fluctuate due to seasonal and rainfall influences and may differ from those observed during the geotechnical investigation.

Tenderers shall make their own assessment of the information provided and allow for all dewatering, groundwater management, excavation support and temporary works necessary to undertake the Works. In accordance with the PPR, all associated costs and risks are the responsibility of the Contractor and shall be deemed included in the Contract Sum. No additional groundwater investigation data is available

publicQuestions.question:
The tender documents identify Donkey Steps as a significant access constraint but do not define construction vehicle limits. Please confirm:

Which access route(s) will be available for construction traffic?

What GVM, axle load, vehicle/trailer dimensions, operating hours and movement restrictions apply?

Can tenderers assume project-specific exemptions will be approved for quarry trucks, concrete agitators, low loaders, drilling/piling plant and large armour rock deliveries?

Are pilot/escort, convoy or wet-weather restrictions applicable?

Must tenderers allow for material transfer/staging and/or access-road maintenance, upgrading or reinstatement?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please find answers to your questions below:

Which access route(s) will be available for construction traffic? - Only one route is available into the valley, via the Donkey Steps access road. The damaged section of Wolgan Road into the Wolgan Valley is closed to all vehicles.

What GVM, axle load, vehicle/trailer dimensions, operating hours and movement restrictions apply? - The current day-to-day limit for vehicles into the Wolgan Valley is 6t GVM, with a maximum length of 8m. However, Council will review and provide exemption to vehicles above this limit that are involved in the works. Tenderers are to include details regarding the plant proposed for the works in Schedule 4 of the tender schedules, and the perceived risks and treatments involved with utilising this plant in Schedule 12.

Can tenderers assume project-specific exemptions will be approved for quarry trucks, concrete agitators, low loaders, drilling/piling plant and large armour rock deliveries? - Yes, as per above.

Are pilot/escort, convoy or wet-weather restrictions applicable? - Council may consider temporary closure of the road to residents whilst heavy plant is traversing the Donkey Steps. Wet weather restrictions are generally not applicable. However, Council may, at its discretion, close the access road in extreme weather events.

Must tenderers allow for material transfer/staging and/or access-road maintenance, upgrading or reinstatement? - There is no mandated requirement for material staging. However, tenderers are to describe their methodology concerning logistics in their response to Schedule 4 of the tender schedules. Council will require tenderers to rectify any damage to the access road. However, general wear and tear is acceptable.

Commencement versus go-live

Does the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represent the required production go-live date for the replacement application, or the commencement of an implementation and transition period? If an implementation period is anticipated, what is Council's target production go-live date?

Catalogue data access

What interfaces does Council's Spydus environment make available to authorised third-party applications for catalogue search and data extraction, including any API, LCF service, MARC export, OAI-PMH or Z39.50/SRU endpoint and do these cover digital collections as well as physical holdings?

Digital content delivery model

For third-party digital content platforms subject to provider DRM restrictions, does Council require digital content to be rendered natively within the application, or is authenticated access with handoff to the provider's platform acceptable?

RFID and self-check integration

publicQuestions.answer:
Commencement versus go-live

Yes, the service commencement date of 21 December 2026 represents the required production go-live date for the replacement application.

Catalogue data access

We have paid for access to the Spydus API and third-party APIs are also permitted. Spydus still has SIP2 connection available, though it is not a preferred option. Spydus has the ability to export MARC records, we have OAI-PMH set up to harvest records into TROVE and I think Sharon’s team use Z39.50 to import MARC records for cataloguing purposes. We certainly use eContent harvesting to import catalogue records from Libby, BorrowBox and Indyreads. Spydus pricing has increased, so it is possible that we won’t be extending our eContent harvesting to cover any of our other providers.

Digital content delivery model

Our eContent providers handle the DRM requirements. We authenticate patron logins via Spydus API or a SIP2 process and loans are then accessed via the provider’s platform.

RFID and self-check integration

We have Designer Clear 2 Column security gates at all branches. Penrith and St Marys have Return Shelves and all branches have V5 Loan Stations. We are currently running with SIP2 integration but are in the process of converting to LCF via API. Tag data encoding format is ISO 28560 (ISO 15693 also available), frequency is 13.56 MHZ and the encoded elements are the Primary identifier and Content Parameter only.

publicQuestions.question:
Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q. Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

A. The number of Threshold 1 and Threshold 2 exceedances will depend on the final trigger levels adopted. As a guide, TMR aims to capture waveform data for responses exceeding those typically generated by a heavy vehicle of approximately 20 tonnes. For video capture, a lower trigger frequency may be appropriate. Suppliers may assume that approximately the largest 1% of responses would be captured, equating to around 16 events per day based on the expected traffic volume of 1600 heavy vehicles per day.

Q. Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

A. The anticipated contract award date is approximately two weeks after the RFQ closing date, subject to evaluation outcomes and internal approvals.

Q Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

A. A temperature sensor resolution of 0.01°C is required. No specific accuracy requirement has been mandated; however, suppliers should provide details of proposed temperature sensors including the accuracy

Q. Can nominal distances and expected (or max/min) measurement ranges for the displacement sensors be provided, and their required accuracy.

A. Pier 5 has a 375mm slotted hole in the expansion joint restraint angle. A longitudinal displacement sensor measurement range of approximately 400 mm, and transverse and vertical displacement sensor measurement ranges of approximately 50 mm are recommended. Suppliers may propose alternative ranges with justification.

Q. For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?

A. Both approaches are acceptable. A camera with integrated ANPR capability is preferred where available; however, the system does not mandate ANPR functionality. The camera should provide image/video footage of sufficient quality to allow manual number plate identification and verification when required.

publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 31/Aug/2026 11:29 AM)

PLease find the answers to your questions.

1. Design and RPEQ certification – Separable Portions 1, 2 and 3

or the HDD works and Northridge Road works, where the Contractor is required to develop the final alignment, bore profile, methodology or other design elements, those elements are to be designed and certified by an appropriately qualified RPEQ.

For conventional pipeline construction, the Contractor may adopt applicable MICC, WSAA and recognised standard drawings/details for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, thrust restraint and associated pipeline construction without preparing a separate project-specific RPEQ design, unless site conditions require departure from those standards.

RPEQ-certified As-Constructed documentation will be required for all Separable Portions, confirming that the completed works have been constructed in accordance with the approved design, applicable standards and any approved design changes.

Where the Contractor proposes an alternative methodology or departure from the nominated standards or drawings, the Contractor shall provide RPEQ design and certification for that alternative prior to construction.

2. Lagoon Creek HDD long section

A detailed long section has not presently been issued.

The HDD Contractor is required to develop and confirm the proposed bore alignment, entry/exit locations and bore profile as part of its methodology. The current scope nominates an approximate minimum cover of 1.5 m beneath the Lagoon Creek bed, subject to the Contractor's proposed bore profile and Council approval.

Council will review whether any additional survey/design information is available and issue this to all tenderers if applicable.

3. SP2 – Council-installed versus Contractor-installed pipework

Council will provide an annotated plan identifying:

existing/Council-installed water main;

limits of Contractor-installed pipework;

This will be issued to all tenderers as an addendum/clarification.

4. Water main trench section – bedding and backfill

Unless specifically detailed otherwise within the Contract documents, conventional water main construction shall be undertaken in accordance with the applicable SEQ Water Supply Code and associated standard drawings, including requirements for trenching, bedding, embedment, backfill, compaction, fittings, thrust restraint and other typical water main construction details.

Where site conditions or the proposed construction methodology require a departure from the applicable SEQ standard details, the Contractor shall develop the alternative detail and provide RPEQ-certified design documentation for MICC review prior to construction.

5. Road pavement restoration

As per item 4 response.

6. Property service connections

No property service connections are included within the Contractor’s scope of works.

The Contractor is required to install the new water main infrastructure only, in accordance with the issued scope, drawings and applicable standards.

All property service connections, including connections from the new water main to existing property services/meters, will be undertaken separately by Mount Isa City Council at a later stage.

Tenderers are therefore not to include any allowance for property service connections within their tendered price.

7. Road crossing carrier/enveloper pipe

The size, material and configuration of any required enveloper/casing pipe are to be determined through the Contractor’s RPEQ-certified design for the Duchess Road crossing.

Tenderers shall consider the requirements applicable to the crossing of the TMR-controlled road corridor, including applicable TMR standards, clearances, loading requirements and approval conditions.

The Contractor’s design shall nominate the proposed carrier pipe, enveloper/casing (where required), bore diameter, depth/cover, entry and exit locations and associated construction methodology.

The final design is to be RPEQ certified and submitted to MICC for review prior to construction. Any required TMR approval shall be obtained prior to commencement of the affected works.

Council are able to provide some images of the types of signs we have across the city; however, we expect some level of site investigation by the consultant will be beneficial to understand the landscape of signage.

Number of templates:

This is a reasonable basis.

Fabrication-ready files:

Council would like templates of final artwork - editable files which includes exact dimensions, bleeds, vector artwork etc.

Yes - council can provide icons where needed and within visual branding guidelines, however there may be additional icons that we need to get assistance with.

No.

In Person either in council offices or in Hobart. Over video call can also be considered for the right candidate.
